Let me analyze this conflict.

Register: "Suzhou Accurate Weigh Co., Ltd. / Suzhou Hope Scale Co., Ltd."
Document: "Suzhou Accurate Weigh Co., Ltd."

The register value contains two companies separated by " / " — a slash-delimited list. The document value contains only the first one. This is a common case in OIML certificates where multiple applicants are listed, and the register (OIML-CS database) captured both, but the extraction from the document only captured one (possibly because the extraction was truncated, or the certificate's visible text lists only one, or the extractor stopped at the first name).

Which is correct? The register is the authoritative OIML-CS database row. The document extraction shows only one name. The question: is this same-entity, different-entity, document-noise, or unverifiable?

Per the rules:
- same-entity: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences
- document-noise: extraction artifacts (address fragments glued into a name, obvious OCR noise) — best_value from register
- different-entity: genuinely different company or person names — best_value = document's
- unverifiable: presumably when we can't tell

Here the document value is a strict subset of the register value. The document name "Suzhou Accurate Weigh Co., Ltd." is exactly the first component of the register's combined value. This isn't a genuinely different company — it's the same company, just that the register includes a second applicant as well. The document's value is likely an incomplete extraction (the " / Suzhou Hope Scale Co., Ltd." part wasn't captured, possibly because the HTML text was truncated — note the document context is truncated mid-tag: "</st").

Given the truncated document context, the second name might have been lost in extraction. The register likely reflects the full legal listing. The best fused value should be the register's fuller value, since the document value is a subset — not a conflict of identity but an incompleteness in extraction.

Verdict: I'd say "document-noise" fits best — the document value is an artifact of incomplete extraction (truncation), and per rules, extraction artifacts → best_value from register. Alternatively "same-entity" — but same-entity rules are about spelling drift etc. The most apt category: the document's extraction dropped part of the value. The register carries the complete value. So verdict = document-noise, best_value = register's value.

Actually, let me reconsider: could the certificate genuinely list only one applicant while the register erroneously added a second? The register ID matches the cert_id in the document (5813), and num matches. The extraction_method is glm-5.3-flash and source_pdf truncated. The document context is clearly truncated mid-sentence, so we cannot verify from the document text whether the second applicant appears. But the register value being a superset strongly suggests the full certificate lists both (register is derived from the official OIML-CS). The document's value is a subset, so it's not a "genuinely different company" — it's the same first company, missing the second.

Verdict options: "same-entity" would imply the two values denote the same entity, which isn't quite right — the register denotes two entities. "document-noise" is about extraction artifacts — the document value is an artifact of truncated extraction. Best_value from register per the rule. That seems the intended answer.

Why sentence: The document name is an exact prefix/subset of the register's dual-applicant listing; the truncation in the extracted text lost the second applicant, so the register's complete value is authoritative.
